title: Writing Tests with AI
description: Automated testing is crucial, but tedious. Learn how to use AI to generate unit tests and edge cases effortlessly.

data.text: Why AI Is Uniquely Good at Test Generation

Writing tests follows very predictable patterns: arrange-act-assert, given-when-then, or describe-it blocks. AI models trained on millions of test files can generate these patterns fluently. Unlike creative coding tasks, test generation benefits from the AI's ability to systematically enumerate edge cases and write assertions with precision.

To generate useful tests, give the AI the function signature, the function body, and the testing framework conventions. Specify the edge cases you want covered. The AI will generate test functions with appropriate assertions.

data.title: Always include in your test prompt:
items: The function or component under test
The testing framework (Jest, Vitest, pytest, JUnit, etc.)
The project's testing conventions (describe/it, test/expect, etc.)
Specific edge cases you want covered (null inputs, empty arrays, boundary values)

data.text: Different testing frameworks have different conventions. Be explicit about which one you use. A prompt for Jest tests will differ significantly from one for pytest. The AI is very good at matching the exact syntax and conventions of the framework you specify.

data.title: Jest test generation prompt
data.content: Using Jest and @testing-library/react, write tests for this SignupForm component. Cover: valid submission, empty email field, password too short, password mismatch, and API error response. Use userEvent for interactions. Mock the API call with jest.fn().
data.code:
Using Jest and `@testing-library/react`, write tests for this `SignupForm` component. Cover:
- Valid submission
- Empty email field
- Password too short
- Password mismatch
- API error response

Use `userEvent` for interactions. Mock the API call with `jest.fn()`.

data.text: One of the most valuable uses of AI for testing is enumerating edge cases you might not think of. Ask the AI: "What edge cases should I test for this function?" It will suggest boundary values, null inputs, empty collections, and error conditions that are easy to overlook when writing tests by hand.

data.title: Ask for edge cases before writing the tests
data.text: Run a quick prompt asking for edge cases first, then use those edge cases in your test generation prompt. This two-step approach produces more comprehensive test coverage than asking for tests directly.

AI works beautifully with test-driven development. Start by describing the behavior you want in plain English, ask the AI to write the test first, watch it fail, then ask the AI to write the minimal implementation to pass. The AI can also help refactor the implementation while keeping the tests passing.

data.title: TDD with AI:
items: Describe the behavior: "I need a function that validates an email address and returns true/false"
Ask for the test first: "Write a Jest test for this that covers valid emails, invalid emails, empty strings, and null"
Run the test — it should fail since there is no implementation yet
Ask for the implementation: "Write the minimum implementation to pass these tests"
Run tests again — they should pass
Refactor if needed: "Now refactor this to use a regex"

data.text: AI can also generate mock data and mock functions. Describe the shape of the data your function needs and ask for realistic test fixtures. For API mocking, describe the endpoint and response shape, and the AI will generate the mock implementation in your framework's syntax.

data.title: Review generated tests carefully
data.text: AI-generated tests can pass even when they are not testing the right thing. Review each assertion to make sure it is actually testing the behavior you care about. A test that passes by accident is worse than no test at all.

AI is also useful for integration and end-to-end tests, though the prompts need more context about your application's architecture. Describe the user flow, the pages involved, and the expected outcomes. For Playwright or Cypress tests, include the selectors and navigation steps.

data.title: Playwright test generation prompt
data.content: Using Playwright with TypeScript, write an end-to-end test for the checkout flow: navigate to /products, click Add to Cart on the first product, go to /cart, click Checkout, fill shipping form (use test data), submit, and verify the order confirmation page shows order number. Use page.route to mock the payment API with a 200 response.
data.code:
Using Playwright with TypeScript, write an end-to-end test for the checkout flow:
1. Navigate to `/products`
2. Click "Add to Cart" on the first product
3. Go to `/cart`
4. Click "Checkout"
5. Fill shipping form (use test data)
6. Submit
7. Verify the order confirmation page shows order number

Use `page.route` to mock the payment API with a 200 response.

data.title: Test generation best practices
points: Specify the testing framework and conventions clearly
Ask for edge cases before asking for the tests themselves
Use TDD: generate failing tests first, then the implementation
Review every assertion — AI tests can pass for the wrong reason
Generate mock data and fixtures alongside the tests
